item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABNT20 KNHC 252341
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 PM EDT Fri Sep 25 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Gonzalo, located just east of the Cabo Verde Islands, and
on Tropical Storm Fay, located well to the west-southwest of the
Azores.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

&&

Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Gonzalo are issued under WMO
header WTNT32 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPAT2.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Gonzalo are issued under WMO
header WTNT22 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMAT2.

$$
Forecaster Pierce/Evans/Beven

item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...FAY WEAKENS OVER THE ATLANTIC OCEAN... As of 9:00 PM GMT Fri Sep 25 the center of Fay was located near 29.8, -43.0 with movement WSW at 5 mph. The minimum central pressure was 1004 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 50 mph.

item.title: Tropical Storm Fay Public Advisory Number 23
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM GMT Fri Sep 25 2026 
000
WTNT31 KNHC 252033
TCPAT1
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Fay Advisory Number  23
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
900 PM GMT Fri Sep 25 2026
 
...FAY WEAKENS OVER THE ATLANTIC OCEAN...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 PM GMT...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...29.8N 43.0W
ABOUT 1075 MI...1730 KM WSW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WSW OR 250 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1004 MB...29.65 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 PM GMT (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Fay was 
located near latitude 29.8 North, longitude 43.0 West. Fay is moving 
toward the west-southwest near 5 mph (7 km/h). A gradual turn to the 
southwest is expected to occur along with an increase in forward 
speed.
 
Maximum sustained winds have weakened to near 50 mph (85 km/h) with 
higher gusts. Gradual weakening is expected to occur for the next 
few days.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 80 miles (130 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1004 mb (29.65 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 AM GMT.
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Beven

item.title: Tropical Storm Fay Forecast Discussion Number 23
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM GMT Fri Sep 25 2026 
167 
WTNT41 KNHC 252033
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Storm Fay Discussion Number  23
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
900 PM GMT Fri Sep 25 2026

The convective organization for Fay has taken a turn downward as 
wind shear and dry air have started to impact the system. The most 
recent TAFB Dvorak fix was a 2.5/35 kt and the objective intensity 
from UW-CIMSS is in the range of 37-47 kt. Therefore, the initial 
intensity has been lowered to 45 kt for this advisory.

The cyclone is expected to gradually weaken as the shear and dry 
air build over the cyclone. The statistical GFS/ECMWF SHIPS 
intensity guidance indicates that the northerly shear will continue 
to increase over the next several hours. The wind shear will make 
it easier for the dry air to penetrate the core of the cyclone and 
hinder the development of convection. The simulated ECMWF and GFS 
satellite imagery show that Fay loses its convection towards the 
end of the weekend, at which point it would become a post-tropical 
remnant low. However it is possible that this could occur sooner 
given the intensity of the wind shear being over 20 kt and mid-level 
relative humidity less than 40 percent. The current NHC intensity 
forecast is in line with the guidance suite including the HCCA and 
GDMI forecast aids.

Fay's initial motion is estimated to be west-southwest, or 250/4 kt 
as the storm is being steered by a subtropical ridge over the 
central Atlantic. The cyclone is expected to continue on a 
west-southwest to southwest heading through the the forecast period 
as the storm continues to weaken and become a vertically shallow 
remnant low steered by the low-level flow. The latest NHC track 
forecast is similar to the previous forecast, however the forward 
speed has been increased. The current forecast is still in good 
agreement with the GDMI ensemble mean and HCCA corrected consensus 
aids.

item.title: Summary for Tropical Storm Gonzalo (AT2/AL072026)
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...GONZALO WEAKENS AS IT CONTINUES NORTHWARD... As of 2:00 AM CVT Sat Sep 26 the center of Gonzalo was located near 16.9, -22.5 with movement N at 9 mph. The minimum central pressure was 1002 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 45 mph.

item.title: Tropical Storm Gonzalo Public Advisory Number 5
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM CVT Sat Sep 26 2026 
692 
WTNT32 KNHC 260232
TCPAT2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Gonzalo Advisory Number   5
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL072026
200 AM CVT Sat Sep 26 2026
 
...GONZALO WEAKENS AS IT CONTINUES NORTHWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM CVT...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...16.9N 22.5W
ABOUT 30 MI...50 KM ENE OF SAL CABO VERDE
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...N OR 360 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1002 MB...29.59 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
The Government of the Cabo Verde Islands has discontinued the
Tropical Storm Warning for all of the Cabo Verde Islands.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM CVT (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Gonzalo was 
located near latitude 16.9 North, longitude 22.5 West. Gonzalo is 
moving toward the north near 9 mph (15 km/h). A northward motion is 
expected to continue this morning, followed by a slower 
north-northwestward motion over the weekend. On the forecast track, 
the center will move away from northeastern portion of the Cabo 
Verde Islands today.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 45 mph (75 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Additional weakening is anticipated. Gonzalo 
could become a post-tropical remnant low or dissipate later today.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 185 miles (295 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1002 mb (29.59 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by the storm are expected to affect the Cabo
Verde Islands through today. These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM CVT.
 
$$
Forecaster D. Zelinsky
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Tropical Storm Gonzalo Forecast Discussion Number 5
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM CVT Sat Sep 26 2026 
000
WTNT42 KNHC 260233
TCDAT2
 
Tropical Storm Gonzalo Discussion Number   5
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL072026
200 AM CVT Sat Sep 26 2026
 
ASCAT-C data valid near 2230 UTC indicated that Gonzalo's
circulation has become poorly defined. At that time, the center of
Gonzalo was severely stretched by about 100 miles from southwest to
northeast. Although the ASCAT did not fully sample the area where
convection associated with Gonzalo is strongest, it did indicate
that the winds have generally decreased since yesterday. Based on
these data and the latest TAFB Dvorak fix, the intensity has been
lowered to 40 kt. It is worth noting that if current trends
continue and the center does not re-form under the convection,
Gonzalo could dissipate later this morning.

Gonzalo still appears to be moving northward, and should continue 
on this track for the next day or so, though the track could jump 
to the northeast temporarily if the center re-forms nearer the deep 
convection. Regardless, models indicate that the remaining 
convection should become disorganized within the next 24 h, which 
would cause the cyclone to become post-tropical. Given the 
environment that Gonzalo is moving into, which will consist of 
increasing shear and cool SSTs, this seems likely. Once it becomes a 
shallow cyclone, the remnants of Gonzalo are expected to meander 
slowly to the north of the Cabo Verde Islands for several days 
before dissipating near the middle of next week.
